title: A quadratic element of the square of an ideal of large colength is a square up to a factor
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter resolve.tex (Resolution of Surfaces)
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file resolve.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that if a nonzero quadratic polynomial in two variables with field coefficients lies in the square of an ideal of colength greater than one, then that quadratic polynomial is a scalar multiple of a square of a linear polynomial (statement lines 3315-3325). The proof (proof lines 3327-3398) analyses the partial derivatives and reduces the first case to an ideal containing a coordinate where degrees can be compared, treats the characteristic two case through derivations of the field, and rules out the remaining configuration by a conormal module argument and a dimension count. H3: a case analysis with a genuine characteristic two argument, written out in full.
